# extrude

Tool to run a composite web application to easily interact with python functions

To install:	`pip install extrude`

See [examples here](https://github.com/i2mint/extrude/tree/master/extrude/examples).

## Test an app from a single command

`extrude.testing` starts the app in the background, waits until it answers, runs your test, and stops the app (and its children) when the test ends, pass or fail. Useful for a Selenium test of a Streamlit front:

```python
from extrude.testing import run_app_test

def test(url):  # drive the page with selenium here
    ...

run_app_test("my_app.py", test)
```

or `python -m extrude.testing my_app.py test_my_app.py` (the script gets the address as `sys.argv[1]` and in `EXTRUDE_APP_URL`). `running_app(...)` is the same as a context manager. Pass `command=` to serve something other than a Streamlit script.

# extrude.base

Build composite web apps (webservice + streamlit front) from python functions.

### Functions

| [`mk_api`](_autosummary/extrude.base.html.md#extrude.base.mk_api)(funcs[, mall])                 | Generates a py2http application with default configuration for extrude.                       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`mk_web_app`](_autosummary/extrude.base.html.md#extrude.base.mk_web_app)(funcs, \*[, api, api_url]) | Generates a front application which will consume a web service exposing a bunch of functions. |
| `run_api`(app, \*\*kwargs)                                                             |                                                                                               |

### extrude.base.mk_api(funcs, mall=None, \*\*kwargs)

Generates a py2http application with default configuration for extrude.

* **Parameters:**
  * **funcs** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)]) – A list of functions.
  * **kwargs** – Any extra keyword argument used to make the py2http application.

```pycon
>>> def foo():
...     pass
...
>>> app = mk_api([foo])
```

### extrude.base.mk_web_app(funcs, , api=None, api_url=None, \*\*kwargs)

Generates a front application which will consume a web service exposing a bunch
of functions.

* **Parameters:**
  * **funcs** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)]) – A list of functions.
  * **api** (`HttpClient`) – The HttpClient object to consume the API.
  * **api_url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The base url of the API to create a HttpClient object in case the
    `api` parameter is not provided. Ignored otherwise
  * **kwargs** – Any extra keyword argument used to make the front application.


# _autosummary/extrude.crude.html.md

# extrude.crude

Control complex python object through strings.
Wrap functions so that the complex arguments can be specified through a string key
that points to the actual python object (which is stored in a session’s memory or
persisted in some fashion).

# extrude.multi_app

Entrypoint for dispatching multiple child applications with a navigation root.

How to prepare an application for dispatch:

### Functions

| [`dispatch_child_apps`](_autosummary/extrude.multi_app.html.md#extrude.multi_app.dispatch_child_apps)(pathnames[, configs])      | Recurses through a Python module to collect objects that can be dispatched to a streamlit app.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`dispatch_child_apps_from_module`](_autosummary/extrude.multi_app.html.md#extrude.multi_app.dispatch_child_apps_from_module)(root_module)   | Takes a root Python module and scans through its immediate children to dispatch functions.       |
| [`dispatch_child_apps_from_root`](_autosummary/extrude.multi_app.html.md#extrude.multi_app.dispatch_child_apps_from_root)(root_dir[, ...]) | Lists the contents of a directory and passes the list to dispatch_child_apps_from_paths.         |
| [`dispatch_raw_module`](_autosummary/extrude.multi_app.html.md#extrude.multi_app.dispatch_raw_module)(spec)                      | Creates a callable that will execute a module when called.                                       |
| [`execute_module_spec`](_autosummary/extrude.multi_app.html.md#extrude.multi_app.execute_module_spec)(spec)                      | Imports a module into the current environment from a module spec and returns the module          |
| [`get_module_spec_from_pathname`](_autosummary/extrude.multi_app.html.md#extrude.multi_app.get_module_spec_from_pathname)(pathname)        | Creates an instance of importlib.machinery.ModuleSpec from a path.                               |
| `mk_dflt_dispatch`(module, configs)                                                             |                                                                                                  |
| `render_root_nav`(app_name_mapping)                                                             |                                                                                                  |
| `set_current_module`(app_name)                                                                  |                                                                                                  |

### extrude.multi_app.dispatch_child_apps(pathnames, configs=None)

Recurses through a Python module to collect objects that can be dispatched to a streamlit app.

* **Parameters:**
  * **pathnames** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – An iterable of files and/or directory to scan through. If a filename
    points to a directory (a package), will look for \_\_init_\_.py within that directory.
  * **configs** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – (Optional) A dict that maps package names with configuration settings,
    allowing you to specify which object to import from the package and what function
    to use to dispatch that object to streamlit.

Example config:
: {“child_pkg_1”: {“import_name”: “funcs_to_dispatch”, “dispatcher”: my_dispatcher}}
  config[pkgname][‘dispatch’] can be a string to refer to a dispatcher within the module,
  or a reference to a callable from the root app. The default dispatcher will be
  streamlitfront.base.dispatch_funcs.

### extrude.multi_app.dispatch_child_apps_from_module(root_module, configs=None)

Takes a root Python module and scans through its immediate children to dispatch functions.

* **Parameters:**
  * **root_module** ([`ModuleType`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/types.html#types.ModuleType)) – A module that contains one or more child packages to dispatch.
  * **configs** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – (Optional) See dispatch_child_apps.

```pycon
>>> import streamlit as st
>>> import extrude.examples.example_apps_simple as example_apps
>>>
>>> # this function call won't work correctly in the test environment
>>> # dispatch_child_apps_from_module(example_apps)
```

### extrude.multi_app.dispatch_child_apps_from_root(root_dir, configs=None)

Lists the contents of a directory and passes the list to dispatch_child_apps_from_paths.

* **Parameters:**
  * **root_dir** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A path to a directory that contains one or more children to dispatch.
  * **configs** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – (Optional) See dispatch_child_apps.

### extrude.multi_app.dispatch_raw_module(spec)

Creates a callable that will execute a module when called.
Used to run a streamlit app without needing to modify it.

* **Parameters:**
  **spec** – importlib.machinery.ModuleSpec

### extrude.multi_app.execute_module_spec(spec)

Imports a module into the current environment from a module spec and returns the module

### extrude.multi_app.get_module_spec_from_pathname(pathname)

Creates an instance of importlib.machinery.ModuleSpec from a path.


# _autosummary/extrude.testing.html.md

# extrude.testing

Run a test against an app in one call: start the app, wait until it answers, run the test, stop the app.

The motivating case is a Selenium test of a Streamlit front: no second terminal, and the
app process (with its children) is gone when the test ends, pass or fail.

```pycon
>>> import sys
>>> serve = lambda app, port: [sys.executable, "-m", "http.server", str(port), "--bind", "127.0.0.1"]
>>> run_app_test("ignored", lambda url: url.startswith("http://"), command=serve, host="127.0.0.1")
True
```

From a shell: `python -m extrude.testing app.py test_app.py` (the test script reads
the app’s address from `sys.argv[1]` or the `EXTRUDE_APP_URL` environment variable).

Stdlib only. Seams: `command=` builds the argv that serves `app` on a port (default:
`streamlit run`), and `popen=` starts it.

### Functions

| [`free_port`](_autosummary/extrude.testing.html.md#extrude.testing.free_port)([host])                                | A port nothing is listening on right now.                                    |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`main`](_autosummary/extrude.testing.html.md#extrude.testing.main)([argv])                                     | `python -m extrude.testing APP TEST`: exit with the test script's exit code. |
| [`run_app_test`](_autosummary/extrude.testing.html.md#extrude.testing.run_app_test)(app, test, \*\*running_app_kwargs)  | Start `app`, run `test` against it, stop the app; return the test's result.  |
| [`running_app`](_autosummary/extrude.testing.html.md#extrude.testing.running_app)(app, \*[, port, command, host, ...]) | Serve `app` in the background and yield its URL once it accepts connections. |
| [`streamlit_command`](_autosummary/extrude.testing.html.md#extrude.testing.streamlit_command)(app, port)                     | The argv that serves the Streamlit script `app` headless on `port`.          |

### extrude.testing.free_port(host='localhost')

A port nothing is listening on right now.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### extrude.testing.main(argv=None)

`python -m extrude.testing APP TEST`: exit with the test script’s exit code.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### extrude.testing.run_app_test(app, test, \*\*running_app_kwargs)

Start `app`, run `test` against it, stop the app; return the test’s result.

* **Parameters:**
  * **test** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – a callable taking the app’s URL (its return value is returned), or the path
    of a Python script, run with the URL as `sys.argv[1]` and in `EXTRUDE_APP_URL`
    (a non-zero exit raises `subprocess.CalledProcessError`; the return is `None`).
  * **running_app_kwargs** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – see [`running_app()`](_autosummary/extrude.testing.html.md#extrude.testing.running_app).
* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

### extrude.testing.running_app(app, \*, port=None, command=<function streamlit_command>, host='localhost', ready_timeout_s=30.0, stop_grace_s=5.0, env=None, cwd=None, popen=<class 'subprocess.Popen'>)

Serve `app` in the background and yield its URL once it accepts connections.

On exit (normal or by exception) the app’s process group is stopped.

* **Parameters:**
  * **app** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – what `command` serves (for the default, the path of a Streamlit script).
  * **port** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the port to serve on; a free one is picked when `None`.
  * **command** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `(app, port) -> argv`; default runs `streamlit run`.
  * **ready_timeout_s** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – how long to wait for the app to answer.
* **Raises:**
  [**RuntimeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError) – the app exited, or never answered; the message carries its output.
* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### extrude.testing.streamlit_command(app, port)

The argv that serves the Streamlit script `app` headless on `port`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]
